methodology.scope: Symbolic music notation and music-document encoding, not audio compression.
methodology.emphasis: Balanced: scholarly editing, notation, analysis, performance and interchange.
assumptions: KRN means Humdrum **kern, not every representation that can inhabit a Humdrum file. Adjacent representations and VHV conventions are labelled.
MusicXML means the published 4.0 specification; a receiving application may implement much less.

MuseScore 4 means the native MSCZ/MSCX project and the application workflows documented for the 4.x family. Exact release differences are retained where known. This is not a frozen source-code audit of one build.
MEI means 5.1 across the full framework; MEI Basic and repertoire-specific customizations can exclude features.
Direct is not a quality score or a promise of render/playback/import support. No format is assigned an overall winner.

All capability assessments are documentation-based or explicitly inferred/unverified. No music-format round-trip, playback or converter tests were run. HTML/data checks are a separate validation activity.
Blank or absent common basics are deliberate: this comparison prioritises distinctions, failure modes and modelling choices.
Sources are primary specifications, maintainer documentation or official application handbooks. Live pages may change; accessed dates are recorded.

evidence.documented: The cited primary documentation states the mechanism or limitation. This does not mean it was empirically tested.
evidence.inference: An author judgement or proposed workflow derived from the cited model; not an explicit guarantee by the specification or vendor.
evidence.unverified: The precise capability was not established. A related source defines the context rather than proving support or absence.

methodology.workflow: Keep the richest appropriate master. Produce task-specific derivatives. Compare semantic events, editorial information, layout and playback independently after conversion.
methodology.coverage_limits: Broad rather than exhaustive. Specialist non-Western notations, electroacoustic spatial scores, braille conversion and full DAW/MIDI 2.0 workflows are outside the detailed matrix. No numerical benchmarks or converter league table are claimed.

formats.name: KRN / Humdrum **kern
formats.baseline: Original **kern, with explicitly labelled VHV/Humdrum extensions
formats.description: A strong fit for corpus work and explicit aligned musical data. Distinguish core **kern from extra spines and rendering conventions.

formats.name: MusicXML
formats.description: A practical exchange format with more editorial and polymetric expressivity than many importing applications expose.

formats.name: MuseScore 4 native
formats.baseline: MSCZ / MSCX; 4.x handbook, with 4.6 family as a reference point
formats.description: The application’s native working score. Strong for layout, linked parts and playback setup; constrained by the application model.

formats.name: Music Encoding Initiative
formats.baseline: MEI 5.1; full framework, with subset caveats
formats.description: Particularly expressive for sources, editorial choices and historical notation. A schema capability is not a renderer guarantee.

direct.label: Direct
direct.description: A documented construct or application workflow expresses this feature within the stated scope.

qualified.label: Qualified
qualified.description: Representable, but a significant semantic, structural, profile or implementation condition applies.

extension.label: Extension
extension.description: Requires a named dialect, adjacent representation or agreed additional vocabulary.

workaround.label: Workaround
workaround.description: Approximate, reframe or externalise the information; some semantics or convenience are lost.

unknown.label: Unverified
unknown.description: The reviewed evidence does not establish the specific capability; a targeted test is needed.

features.question: The design centre predicts which information is natural to preserve.

krn.mechanism: Humdrum coordinates typed spines; **kern supplies a compact musical vocabulary.

musicxml.mechanism: MusicXML exchanges score notation and selected performance information between applications.

musescore.mechanism: MSCZ/MSCX preserve the score as a MuseScore project, with application-specific editing and presentation state.

mei.mechanism: MEI models musical documents, their interpretation and their documentary context.

features.feature: Version and dialect are part of the answer
features.question: A filename extension alone does not specify a reproducible interpretation.

krn.mechanism: Separate original **kern from VHV/humlib conventions and other Humdrum representations.
krn.caveat: A signifier can acquire different practical meanings; record the dialect.

musicxml.mechanism: This comparison uses the published 4.0 specification, not an evolving editor draft.

musescore.mechanism: Application and file versions differ: the documented 4.6.x family uses native file version 4.60.
musescore.caveat: Live handbook claims need checking against the exact installed build.

mei.mechanism: CMN, Mensural, Neumes, All and Basic are distinct schema choices.
mei.caveat: Full MEI capabilities cannot be assumed for MEI Basic.

features.question: This changes parsing, editing and comparison algorithms.

krn.mechanism: Events align across tab-separated spines; null tokens carry no new event. Split/join operations change spine topology.

musicxml.mechanism: Durations advance a cursor; backup/forward coordinate voices and staves inside a measure.

musescore.mechanism: Editing follows a shared measure structure and four voice slots per staff.

mei.mechanism: CMN normally nests measure → staff → layer; control events can target notes through identifiers or timestamps.

features.feature: Stable addresses for notes and annotations
features.question: Can an external comment keep pointing to the same musical object after edits?

krn.mechanism: Plain tokens do not provide a universal durable note ID; add identifiers in associated data.
krn.caveat: Line/field offsets change during editing.

musicxml.mechanism: Optional element IDs and bookmark targets can identify locations.
musicxml.caveat: Importer preservation and ID stability are separate questions.

musescore.mechanism: No stable public scholarly note-address contract was established from the documentation reviewed.
musescore.caveat: Do not use screen position as a durable identifier.

mei.mechanism: xml:id supports references; corresp, sameas and related links express relationships.
mei.caveat: An editing workflow must preserve identifiers.

features.question: A file can carry custom data without other programs understanding it.

krn.mechanism: Define another exclusive interpretation and align its values with the music.
krn.caveat: Document the vocabulary and the programs that understand it.

musicxml.mechanism: other-notation and related fields carry additional vocabulary.
musicxml.caveat: Custom text alone does not establish interoperable semantics.

musescore.mechanism: Use project metadata or visible text for project-specific information.
musescore.caveat: Arbitrary new native XML elements are not a supported interchange contract.

mei.mechanism: Choose or customize a schema for the project.
mei.caveat: Distribute the customization; a generic MEI reader may not implement it.

features.question: This is an engineering judgement about the representation, not a file-size benchmark.

krn.mechanism: Text rows are concise; adding a spine changes many lines and alignment.

musicxml.mechanism: XML is reviewable; changed voice order, divisions or layout can create large non-musical diffs.

musescore.mechanism: Compressed projects are awkward to diff; inspect XML where available and retain original packages.

mei.mechanism: XML structure and identifiers support targeted comparison; different valid encodings can still differ substantially.

features.question: Distinguish a title field from a description of a physical source.

krn.mechanism: Standard !!! records cover authorship and bibliographic data; project-defined records can supplement them.

musicxml.mechanism: identification includes creators, rights, encoding history, source and relations; miscellaneous fields add metadata.

musescore.mechanism: Project Properties provides descriptive tags, including custom tags; visible title text is a separate object.

mei.mechanism: meiHead distinguishes the encoding, work, sources and revision history; source descriptions support bibliographic scholarship.

features.question: Saving a score is different from preserving every dependency needed to reproduce it.

krn.mechanism: Preserve dialect definitions and rendering/conversion versions with the text.

musicxml.mechanism: Layout and font defaults are encoded, but omitted defaults are application decisions.
musicxml.caveat: Keep referenced resources and a reference rendering.

musescore.mechanism: Rendering fonts and playback sounds/plugins belong to the reproducibility environment.
musescore.caveat: A project does not guarantee identical output on another installation.

mei.mechanism: Facsimile and recording references can point outside the XML.
mei.caveat: Archive those resources and the schema/rendering profile.

features.question: Encode both the musical alteration and its editorial status.

krn.mechanism: Declare an editorial-accidental signifier, commonly i, in !!!RDF**kern.
krn.caveat: This is a named convention, not a universal meaning of the letter i.

musicxml.mechanism: accidental separates the printed symbol from pitch alteration; editorial, bracket and parentheses convey its treatment.
musicxml.caveat: Importer support must be tested.

musescore.mechanism: Accidental/notehead enclosures can mark an intervention visually.
musescore.caveat: A bracket does not itself identify an editor, source or conjecture.

mei.mechanism: accid records accidental information; supplied and responsibility markup can state an editorial intervention.

features.question: Preserve the reason a reading differs from the apparent source.

krn.mechanism: Original **kern defines Y, x, X and ? for editorial distinctions.
krn.caveat: Modern VHV uses X for forced accidental display; declare conventions before mixing encodings.

musicxml.mechanism: level carries editorial status text and enclosure attributes.
musicxml.caveat: No equivalent typed hierarchy of sic/corr alternatives is supplied here.

musescore.mechanism: Explain editorial categories with text, styles or a separate apparatus.
musescore.caveat: Readers cannot infer a scholarly ontology from colour or italics.

mei.mechanism: sic/corr and orig/reg express distinct editorial acts; choice can retain both alternatives.

features.question: Alternatives should remain alternatives, rather than simultaneous performed notes.

krn.mechanism: Humdrum strophes can retain alternative versions.
krn.caveat: Witness relationships and reading selection need a documented project model.

musicxml.mechanism: Keep the selected score and describe variants in footnotes or linked material.
musicxml.caveat: An ossia is not a general critical apparatus.

musescore.mechanism: Use separate scores/staves and an external apparatus for witness comparisons.
musescore.caveat: Avoid making every reading sound simultaneously.

mei.mechanism: A critical apparatus groups lemma and readings with source attribution.
mei.caveat: A renderer needs a reading-selection policy.

features.question: Who supplied this note, rather than who edited the whole file?

krn.mechanism: Attach responsibility using a defined annotation convention; reference records identify contributors at document level.

musicxml.mechanism: Associate a note with explanatory level/footnote content or external attribution.
musicxml.caveat: Use an explicit project convention for machine-readable responsibility.

musescore.mechanism: Project creator tags do not establish per-intervention scholarly responsibility.
musescore.workaround: Maintain an apparatus keyed to score locations.

mei.mechanism: Responsibility attributes can identify the person or agency responsible for an editorial act.

features.question: An uncertain reading is not simply an invisible or small note.

krn.mechanism: Record confidence in comments or an associated spine under a project convention.

musicxml.mechanism: Explain uncertainty using editorial level/footnote text; retain any numeric model externally.

musescore.mechanism: Use notation/text for readers and an external record for structured confidence.

mei.mechanism: Editorial markup can carry qualitative certainty and, on applicable elements, numeric confidence.
mei.caveat: Check attribute availability in the selected customization.

features.question: A lost passage, an unreadable passage and an editorial completion are different claims.

krn.summary: Do not use rests for loss
krn.mechanism: Represent loss through a declared annotation convention; distinguish musical silence from missing evidence.

musicxml.mechanism: A performance rest does not mean a damaged source; explain the gap and any reconstruction separately.

musescore.mechanism: Retain damage information outside the sounding reconstruction or in visible notes.

mei.mechanism: Different elements distinguish omission, uncertain reading and editorial replacement; attributes qualify extent and cause.

features.question: Describe changes on the manuscript, not only the editor’s final reading.

krn.mechanism: Alternative streams and annotations can document revisions under a local model.
krn.caveat: No claim of a standard genetic-editing ontology.

musicxml.mechanism: Use links or supplementary documentation for manuscript operations.
musicxml.caveat: Score editing history is not manuscript revision history.

musescore.mechanism: Application edits produce a score; document scribal/compositional revisions separately.

mei.mechanism: MEI distinguishes visible source changes from editorial correction and supports genetic textual work.

features.question: Keep original and regularized forms together without overwriting the source.

krn.mechanism: Use alternative sections/strophes or documented original/modernized conventions.
krn.caveat: Extraction rules must specify which view is intended.

musicxml.mechanism: Store separate score versions or linked originals and explanations.
musicxml.caveat: A selected appearance alone does not retain both interpretations.

musescore.mechanism: Maintain distinct views and document how edits propagate.
musescore.caveat: Linked performance parts are not editorial-choice containers.

mei.mechanism: Retain original and regularized encodings within a choice.
mei.caveat: Rendering/extraction software must choose a branch.

features.feature: Link notes to manuscript image regions
features.question: A URL to a page is weaker than a coordinate-based relationship to a note.

krn.mechanism: Use note-address conventions and image-region references in associated metadata.

musicxml.mechanism: link/bookmark can associate resources and locations.
musicxml.caveat: Image zones and surface relationships require a project convention.

musescore.mechanism: An image or URL in a project is not a semantic note-to-surface mapping.
musescore.workaround: Keep coordinate and identity mapping externally.

mei.mechanism: Define source surfaces and zones; musical elements can reference them with facs.

features.question: Distinguish a printed comment from an addressable scholarly assertion.

krn.mechanism: Local/global comments and typed spines permit annotation; define the target and vocabulary explicitly.

musicxml.mechanism: footnote supports printed commentary; grouping/feature supports analysis.
musicxml.caveat: These are different mechanisms with different consumers.

musescore.mechanism: Use visible comments or an external structured annotation file.
musescore.caveat: Score text is not a general annotation graph.

mei.mechanism: annot can carry explanation, attribution and links to affected material.

features.question: A scholarly edition may need to describe an object, not merely cite its title.

krn.mechanism: Reference records identify sources; detailed material description needs additional conventions.

musicxml.mechanism: identification/source supplies bibliographic context.
musicxml.caveat: Detailed codicology requires external or project-specific metadata.

musescore.mechanism: Keep detailed physical-source and hand descriptions alongside the score.

mei.mechanism: MEI metadata covers physical sources and provenance with detailed source-description structures.

features.feature: Producing a performable reading from an edition
features.question: Retaining alternatives and selecting one for playback are separate operations.

krn.mechanism: Section and strophe tools can select an interpretation before further processing.

musicxml.mechanism: The interchange score generally represents a chosen musical text.
musicxml.caveat: Preserve the apparatus elsewhere if selecting loses evidence.

musescore.mechanism: Create a playing score from the selected reading; keep documentary information outside that reduction.

mei.mechanism: app/choice preserve alternatives; consumers must define which reading becomes the score.
mei.caveat: Schema validity does not determine an editorial policy.

features.feature: Two independent voices on one stave
features.question: Represent independent rhythms and voice identity, not just a chord with opposite stems.

krn.mechanism: *^ and *v split and join streams; VHV interprets subspines as voices sharing a staff.
krn.caveat: Staff rendering belongs to the consumer’s conventions.

musicxml.mechanism: Use separate voice labels, the same staff number and cursor movement to encode overlapping lines.

musescore.mechanism: Enter the lines in separate voice slots on the same staff.
musescore.caveat: Stem direction alone does not establish a separate voice.

mei.mechanism: Each voice occupies a layer inside the same staff.

features.feature: More than four independent voices per stave
features.question: A schema-level capability can exceed a notation application’s internal model.

krn.mechanism: Spine splitting is not limited to four branches by the Humdrum syntax.
krn.caveat: Rendering complexity and tool limits remain.

musicxml.mechanism: voice contains a string; the format does not prescribe MuseScore’s four slots.
musicxml.caveat: Destination programs may merge or redistribute voices.

musescore.mechanism: The documented model permits four voices.
musescore.workaround: Use extra staves or reorganise the notation; retain original voice identities separately.

mei.mechanism: MEI does not impose a four-layer limit analogous to MuseScore’s voice slots.
mei.caveat: Check the target renderer.

features.question: Preserve continuity through a passage that branches and later rejoins.

krn.mechanism: Spine split/join operations describe branching and convergence.

musicxml.mechanism: Use voice labels and aligned events; a merge is inferred from subsequent voice use.
musicxml.caveat: No general voice-lineage graph is implied.

musescore.mechanism: Voice slots allow local polyphony; staff additions are a separate layout choice.
musescore.caveat: Four slots remain the ceiling.

mei.mechanism: Layers and linking attributes can distinguish musical material and its correspondence.
mei.caveat: Define how lineage should be interpreted.

features.question: Logical voice ownership need not equal the staff on which a note is drawn.

krn.mechanism: Staff assignment and layout conventions supplement the core stream representation.
krn.caveat: Test cross-staff conversion in the chosen Humdrum renderer.

musicxml.mechanism: staff and voice distinguish location from voice identity; beaming is specified separately.

musescore.mechanism: Cross-staff movement keeps logical ownership on the original staff.
musescore.caveat: Moving one note moves the whole chord.

mei.mechanism: Events can identify a staff independently of their containment; cross-staff beam attributes describe the relation.

features.question: This is narrower than moving an entire voice to another stave.

krn.mechanism: The exact shared-stem, split-chord result was not verified for the selected Humdrum renderer.

musicxml.mechanism: The notation tutorial demonstrates chord members assigned to different staves.

musescore.mechanism: The handbook says individual members of a chord cannot be moved independently across staves.
musescore.workaround: Separate the members into voices and adjust the stems/beams.

mei.mechanism: The data model provides staff assignment on individual notes.
mei.caveat: Shared-stem rendering and import need a fixture test.

features.question: Do not silently flatten independently sustained notes into a single uniform chord.

krn.mechanism: Represent independent continuations in subspines rather than relying on a mixed-duration chord token.

musicxml.mechanism: A chord member may be shorter, but not longer, than the preceding anchor note.
musicxml.caveat: Separate voices are clearer for independent subsequent motion.

musescore.mechanism: Use different voice slots when simultaneous notes have different rhythmic continuations.

mei.mechanism: The chord definition specifies equal duration; use layers for independent durations.
mei.caveat: Do not assume every schema-permitted note attribute defines a supported mixed-duration chord.

features.feature: Ossia and alternatives on small staves
features.question: An alternate passage is not simply a second part playing at the same time.

krn.mechanism: Humdrum alternatives can retain alternate passages; engraved ossia treatment is consumer-specific.

musicxml.mechanism: staff-details permits staff types, sizes and visibility choices.
musicxml.caveat: Selection and non-playing behaviour need explicit handling.

musescore.mechanism: Use an additional staff, adjust size and hide unused regions.
musescore.caveat: Check playback and part inclusion.

mei.mechanism: CMN includes ossia; it is distinct from the critical apparatus.
mei.caveat: Renderer support varies.

features.question: Representing a part differs from maintaining synchronised editable views.

krn.mechanism: Part extraction is a transformation of the encoded streams.
krn.caveat: Independent engraving edits need separate management.

musicxml.mechanism: Score and part data can be exchanged, but the format does not mandate a live linked editing session.

musescore.mechanism: Custom parts can show selected instruments and voices, with their own styles.
musescore.caveat: Exporting the parts is not the same as transferring the native linkage.

mei.mechanism: MEI can describe score and part structures and their relationships.
mei.caveat: Live synchronisation is an application responsibility.

features.feature: Different metres over a shared bar span
features.question: Example: 18/16 in one staff against 3/4 in another, with coincident barlines.

krn.mechanism: Meter indications can differ by spine; encode durations so synchronisation is explicit.
krn.caveat: Different labels alone do not rescale elapsed time.

musicxml.mechanism: time/@number scopes the signature; actual durations and time modification must express the common span.
musicxml.caveat: The numerator alone does not determine a tempo ratio.

musescore.mechanism: Local signatures stretch the notated content into the global bar span, like an invisible tuplet.

mei.mechanism: staffDef can hold a distinct meter; durations/proportions must establish the intended synchronisation.
mei.caveat: Validate the rendering and temporal interpretation.

features.question: Example: 3/4 and 4/4 at the same quarter-note pulse; barlines meet every 12 quarters.

krn.mechanism: The documented VHV polymeter example inserts barline records at the combined boundaries and uses invisible =- in unaffected spines.
krn.caveat: These extra structural boundaries can affect analysis.

musicxml.mechanism: Partwise measures support non-controlling="yes" for a left boundary not aligned with other parts.
musicxml.caveat: The flag describes the left boundary. Receiving applications may still force common measure boundaries.

musescore.mechanism: Local time signatures keep the global bar duration.
musescore.workaround: Use a common subdivision grid or longer shared containers, hide unwanted boundaries and draw local barlines where needed. Repair numbering and retain local bar identities separately.

mei.mechanism: barLine/control and measure control distinguish alignment points; part-oriented or unmeasured structures can express independent boundaries.
mei.caveat: On measure, control describes the right boundary. Shared measure containers may need restructuring; renderer support is not assured.

features.question: Different printed tempo marks are not proof of independently running clocks.

krn.mechanism: Tandem interpretations can differ across spines.
krn.caveat: Common record alignment still needs a declared temporal interpretation.
krn.workaround: Use a common time grid or external performance model.

musicxml.mechanism: Tempo directions can be written, but independent concurrent playback clocks were not established.
musicxml.workaround: Encode rational ratios on a shared timeline or retain separate performance data.

musescore.mechanism: Use tuplets and explicit notation for rational ratios; independent clocks need a separate performance workflow.

mei.mechanism: Gestural and real-time attributes can describe timing distinct from notation.
mei.caveat: This does not promise polytempo playback in a renderer.

features.question: Removing visible barlines is different from removing a measure-based data model.

krn.mechanism: Event streams can omit barlines; durations remain available for analysis.

musicxml.mechanism: A time element may specify senza-misura.
musicxml.caveat: Music still lives in measure containers; choose boundaries deliberately.

musescore.mechanism: Hide signatures/barlines, or create irregular measures.
musescore.caveat: The score still behaves as measures internally.

mei.mechanism: MEI supports music organised without CMN measure containers, including historical repertoires.

features.question: Nominal metre, actual duration and displayed numbering should stay distinct.

krn.mechanism: Durations and bar markers are explicit; metre-conformance checks remain separate.

musicxml.mechanism: implicit can suppress the measure number; encoded events determine content rather than the printed number alone.

musescore.mechanism: Measure properties allow an actual duration differing from the time signature.

mei.mechanism: metcon identifies whether a measure conforms to the prevailing metre.
mei.caveat: It does not by itself supply the missing duration.

features.question: A display such as 3+2/8 or 2/4+3/8 should not obscure the duration model.

krn.mechanism: Use meter interpretations and supported display conventions.
krn.caveat: Distinguish computational metre from its visual spelling.

musicxml.mechanism: Additive numerators and multiple beat units have explicit encodings.

musescore.mechanism: Time-signature properties control display and beaming.
musescore.caveat: Unusual denominators and exact playback should be tested in the chosen build.

mei.mechanism: MEI meter counts permit expressions; grouped signatures extend the notation model.

features.question: The sounding ratio and the visible bracket hierarchy are separate information.

krn.mechanism: Reciprocal durations express timing; VHV adds controls for displayed tuplets.
krn.caveat: Do not assume bracket hierarchy is recoverable from duration alone.

musicxml.mechanism: time-modification gives cumulative scaling; tuplet describes the displayed and nested structure.

musescore.mechanism: The editor supports user-defined ratios and nested groups.
musescore.caveat: Test unusual ratios during interchange.

mei.mechanism: MEI offers tuplet grouping and span-based descriptions.
mei.caveat: Use the appropriate construction for containment and overlap.

features.question: A duration ratio may be representable even when an editor cannot keep one bracket across a bar.

krn.mechanism: Rhythmic values can continue across bar markers; preservation of one cross-bar tuplet object was not verified.

musicxml.mechanism: Tuplet start/stop markers are not a nested measure container.
musicxml.caveat: Cross-bar rendering and import require a test.

musescore.mechanism: The handbook documents nesting but does not establish arbitrary cross-bar tuplets.
musescore.workaround: Consider a longer measure with visual subdivision, documenting the structural compromise.

mei.mechanism: The dedicated span element explicitly targets tuplets extending across barlines.

features.question: Grace-note appearance does not uniquely determine the performance duration.

krn.mechanism: Core **kern distinguishes grace material; exact realised timing needs additional performance information.

musicxml.mechanism: grace offers make-time and percentages stolen from preceding or following notes.

musescore.mechanism: Before/after grace notes attach to a main note and do not count towards the measure.
musescore.caveat: Playback is an engine interpretation, not a complete performance transcript.

mei.mechanism: grace and grace.time distinguish grace treatment; gestural timing can supplement the written duration.

features.question: A compact written score and an expanded performance sequence are different representations.

krn.mechanism: Humdrum sections and expansion mechanisms can specify performance order.
krn.caveat: Preserve the compact source when making an expanded derivative.

musicxml.mechanism: Barline/ending notation and sound jump attributes serve related but distinct purposes.

musescore.mechanism: Repeats are part of the score workflow; intricate jumps should be checked by listening and export.

mei.mechanism: MEI supports structural sections and expansion mechanisms.
mei.caveat: Realised order depends on a processing policy.

features.question: Transposing parts can preserve spelling while using different pitch coordinates.

krn.mechanism: **kern records sounding pitch; *ITr describes how to produce a transposed written part.

musicxml.mechanism: transpose specifies the interval added to written pitch to obtain sounding pitch.

musescore.mechanism: The application provides concert-pitch and transposed views.
musescore.caveat: Keep instrument transposition distinct from actually transposing the notes.

mei.mechanism: staffDef transposition and note gestural attributes distinguish written and sounding descriptions.

features.question: A sharp in the encoding does not necessarily mean a printed sharp symbol.

krn.mechanism: Every pitch carries its alteration; VHV computes visibility, with X/y display controls.
krn.caveat: Suppressing a symbol must not erase its pitch alteration.

musicxml.mechanism: Pitch alteration and the actual printed accidental are distinct elements.

musescore.mechanism: Notation controls coexist with playback tuning and note properties.
musescore.caveat: Verify cautionary-symbol import separately from sounding pitch.

mei.mechanism: Written and gestural inflections can differ.

features.question: A quarter-tone glyph, an exact pitch and its playback are three separate tests.

krn.mechanism: **cents can express fractional-semitone values alongside **kern.
krn.caveat: That is Humdrum extensibility, not native microtonal **kern spelling.

musicxml.mechanism: alter permits decimal values; the accidental vocabulary supplies notational symbols.
musicxml.caveat: Playback and uncommon glyph support vary.

musescore.mechanism: Note properties offer playback tuning in cents.
musescore.caveat: Sound-engine behaviour is version-dependent and untested here; do not infer it from the symbol.

mei.mechanism: Accidental vocabularies and gestural pitch support distinctions beyond ordinary semitone notation.
mei.caveat: Exact tuning and glyph rendering depend on profile and consumer.

features.question: A note name alone does not determine a frequency without a tuning model.

krn.mechanism: **freq explicitly encodes hertz; it can coexist with symbolic notation.

musicxml.mechanism: Decimal alterations encode offsets, but a general temperament system is not supplied by that field alone.
musicxml.workaround: Document the tuning reference and conversion rules.

musescore.mechanism: Cents adjustments can implement a tuning in compatible playback setups.
musescore.caveat: Retain tuning assumptions and test the sound engine.

mei.mechanism: staffDef includes tune.Hz, tune.pname and tune.temper.
mei.caveat: The consumer must implement the specified tuning.

features.question: A key signature is neither the same as a tonal analysis nor a complete tuning system.

krn.mechanism: **kern separates key-signature interpretation from key designation.
krn.caveat: Unusual glyph placement is a rendering matter.

musicxml.mechanism: key supports both conventional fifths and explicit altered steps, with staff scoping.

musescore.mechanism: The editor supports customised key signatures and local application.
musescore.caveat: Check nonstandard accidentals against playback and export.

mei.mechanism: Nonstandard signatures use keySig rather than only a conventional signature abbreviation.

features.question: Preserve the distinction between sounding pitch, fingering and notated string instructions.

krn.mechanism: **fret and associated tuning interpretations describe fretted instruments.
krn.caveat: This extends beyond core **kern.

musicxml.mechanism: scordatura/accord describe altered strings; staff-details carries tuning and capo information.

musescore.mechanism: From 4.2, tuning instructions affect a staff and linked staves from their measure onward.
musescore.caveat: Check written scordatura conventions separately.

mei.mechanism: Tablature distinguishes notated courses from physical strings and describes their tuning.

features.question: A note’s height on the staff need not represent a sounding pitch.

krn.mechanism: Humdrum rendering uses percussion conventions for pitch, head shape and instrument interpretation.
krn.caveat: Do not treat staff position as an ordinary tonal pitch.

musicxml.mechanism: unpitched uses display-step/display-octave; instrument information supplies the playback identity.

musescore.mechanism: Percussion notation relies on the configured instrument and staff model.
musescore.caveat: A decorative percussion glyph alone has no playback semantics.

mei.mechanism: Staff location and instrument/performance information can be encoded separately.
mei.caveat: Check percussion mappings in the consumer.

features.feature: Mensural notation as a semantic system
features.question: A mensuration sign can govern duration rather than merely decorate a modern time signature.

krn.mechanism: Humdrum has a separate **mens representation for mensural signs, durations and related features.
krn.caveat: Label this as an adjacent representation, not a core KRN capability.

musicxml.mechanism: Use modern durations and visual approximations, retaining mensural interpretation externally.
musicxml.caveat: A historical glyph does not introduce mensural duration semantics.

musescore.mechanism: The handbook describes mensural signs as display-only substitutions over conventional metre.
musescore.caveat: They do not change the duration ratios between note values.

mei.mechanism: MEI models mensuration, proportion and context-sensitive duration distinctions.

features.question: Historical grouping and duration qualification should survive modern transcription.

krn.mechanism: The separate mensural representation includes ligatures, coloration and duration qualifications.

musicxml.mechanism: Retain the historical interpretation in supplemental data if exchanging a modernised score.

musescore.mechanism: Use symbols or a modern transcription with commentary.
musescore.caveat: Do not claim a native mensural semantic model.

mei.mechanism: The mensural module distinguishes notation signs and interpreted durations.
mei.caveat: Not all renderers infer duration from context.

features.question: A modern pitch transcription may discard neume grouping and textual organisation.

krn.mechanism: Core **kern is not a dedicated neume vocabulary.
krn.workaround: Keep grouping and source signs in supplemental data.

musicxml.mechanism: Generic extensions can retain labels/glyphs but do not establish a neume model.

musescore.mechanism: Hide conventional bars and use symbols as needed.
musescore.caveat: The underlying structure remains a notation-editor score.

mei.mechanism: The neumes module organises chant around syllables and neume components.

features.question: String/course assignment can contain information not recoverable from pitch alone.

krn.mechanism: Humdrum provides a separate fret representation; core **kern alone does not preserve every fingering.

musicxml.mechanism: Tablature information is supported; staff-details includes letter/number fret presentation.
musicxml.caveat: Historical idioms require specific interoperability tests.

musescore.mechanism: Create tab staves, including links to standard notation.
musescore.caveat: Check whether a particular historical tab style is supported.

mei.mechanism: MEI describes guitar and Italian, French and German lute tablatures.

features.question: Figures changing during a sustained note need their own temporal placement.

krn.mechanism: VHV documents figured-bass encodings independent of the **kern notes.

musicxml.mechanism: A duration permits figure changes beneath one note; figures retain vertical order.

musescore.mechanism: Specialised entry parses and aligns figures and continuations.
musescore.caveat: This is more semantic than typing ordinary text.

mei.mechanism: MEI harmonic markup distinguishes figures from note events.
mei.caveat: Realising a continuo accompaniment is another operation.

features.feature: Chord symbols, Roman numerals and analysis
features.question: A sounding chord, a printed chord name and an analytical assertion are different objects.

krn.mechanism: **harm models functional harmony; other typed spines can record other analyses.

musicxml.mechanism: MusicXML 4.0 supports chord roots, scale-degree numerals and stacked functional relationships.

musescore.mechanism: Dedicated modes parse chord labels; formatting and playback depend on the kind of symbol.

mei.mechanism: Harmonic and analytical information can coexist with the score and linking relationships.

features.question: Text may be attached to notes or maintained as a separate aligned stream.

krn.mechanism: **text and **silbe support word/syllable-oriented lyrics alongside the music.

musicxml.mechanism: lyric includes syllabic division, elision and extension, with verse identifiers.

musescore.mechanism: Syllabic entry supports extension lines and multiple lyric lines.
musescore.caveat: Keep independent text editions outside a purely graphical lyric layout.

mei.mechanism: Syllables can be encoded within notes or separately and linked to the music.

features.question: Identical-looking curves can assert different musical relationships.

krn.mechanism: **kern separates ties, slurs and phrases; it does not simply record an uninterpreted curved line.

musicxml.mechanism: tie and tied distinguish sound from appearance; analytical grouping is separate.

musescore.mechanism: Use functional notation objects when possible.
musescore.caveat: A decorative symbol or line does not establish the intended musical relation.

mei.mechanism: phrase is available alongside tie and slur, including control of its shape and endpoints.

features.question: Being able to display a glyph is weaker than knowing what it means.

krn.mechanism: Custom representations can carry new meaning; renderer-specific layout must be supplied separately.

musicxml.mechanism: SMuFL-named symbols can be identified; unrestricted custom content does not guarantee interoperability.

musescore.mechanism: The Symbols palette contains non-functional graphical items.
musescore.caveat: They have no effect beyond appearance.

mei.mechanism: User-defined symbols and references can preserve visual information.
mei.caveat: A custom symbol still needs a semantic definition and a capable renderer.

features.question: A static chord diagram is not a time-ordered sequence of string events.

krn.mechanism: **fret describes performance positions; preserve a static diagram separately if required.

musicxml.mechanism: frame represents a fretboard diagram associated with a harmony.

musescore.mechanism: Fretboard-diagram workflows accompany guitar notation.
musescore.caveat: Exact diagram interchange was not tested.

mei.mechanism: Tablature covers course/string information; equivalent static diagram handling needs a selected profile and tool.

features.question: Encoding a break does not guarantee identical pagination in another engine.

krn.mechanism: VHV rendering conventions supplement the symbolic stream.
krn.caveat: Core **kern is not a page-layout language.

musicxml.mechanism: print supplies local page/system/staff parameters; defaults supplies score-wide choices.
musicxml.caveat: Engravers may calculate different spacing.

musescore.mechanism: System breaks and spacing controls are retained in the project.
musescore.caveat: Interchange may recalculate the result.

mei.mechanism: MEI offers layout descriptions; rendering remains a separate process.
mei.caveat: Source breaks and desired output breaks should be distinguished.

features.question: Preserving musical meaning is not a promise of pixel-identical output.

krn.mechanism: The notation output depends on the selected rendering conventions and implementation.

musicxml.mechanism: Applications may reflow even when importing page/system breaks.
musicxml.caveat: Archive PDF/SVG for the approved appearance.

musescore.mechanism: Native controls preserve intent; fonts and application changes can alter output.
musescore.workaround: Keep a rendered reference and record the application build.

mei.mechanism: Facsimiles preserve source images; semantic encoding alone does not fix all rendering choices.

features.feature: Music fonts, glyph identity and fallbacks
features.question: The same glyph identifier may have different metrics or visual forms.

krn.mechanism: Core stream semantics do not dictate a music-font implementation.

musicxml.mechanism: Font defaults and glyph identifiers carry appearance preferences.
musicxml.caveat: Installed fonts and fallbacks still affect rendering.

musescore.mechanism: MuseScore 4.6 introduced loading any compatible SMuFL music font; fallback glyphs may be used.

mei.mechanism: MEI records glyph authorities/names and custom symbols where applicable.
mei.caveat: Preserve the resource and font environment.

features.question: Invisible notation can still affect time, playback and spacing.

krn.mechanism: y can identify logically present but unprinted material; styling conventions add cue treatment.
krn.caveat: Visibility and silence must not be conflated.

musicxml.mechanism: note includes print and playback-related properties; cue notes have specific structural rules.
musicxml.caveat: Test cue playback rather than relying on size alone.

musescore.mechanism: Staves can be hidden when empty or selectively shown.
musescore.caveat: Hidden does not automatically mean removed from every part or playback context.

mei.mechanism: Visibility and cue properties are available in the notation model.
mei.caveat: Some visibility definitions address aural as well as graphical rendering; check the consumer.

features.feature: Beam grouping, feathering and cross-bar beams
features.question: Grouping, geometry and realised acceleration should be evaluated separately.

krn.mechanism: **kern records beaming; detailed placement and uncommon beam forms require renderer conventions.

musicxml.mechanism: beam records grouping and feathering direction; it does not alone define a performed accelerando curve.

musescore.mechanism: Beaming can override time-signature defaults; appearance is adjustable.
musescore.caveat: Check feathered playback separately.

mei.mechanism: Spanning beams can be encoded across barlines without forcing simple tree containment.

features.feature: Spanner endpoints, curvature and open ties
features.question: A curve’s visual endpoint may differ from its musical or performance target.

krn.mechanism: Core slur/tie signifiers carry relationships; fine geometry needs added conventions.

musicxml.mechanism: tied supports drawn ties, including let-ring and ties attached to one note.
musicxml.caveat: A sound tie is a separate element.

musescore.mechanism: Application-specific appearance controls may require adjustment after interchange.
musescore.caveat: Verify both anchors and shape in the target.

mei.mechanism: Control events can carry endpoints and Bezier/bulge descriptions.
mei.caveat: A renderer may not implement all geometry.

features.question: Part layout is not simply a cropped view of the full score.

krn.mechanism: Extract streams and maintain part-specific layout settings alongside them.

musicxml.mechanism: Individual part exports can carry their own layout.
musicxml.caveat: Live linkage to the full-score project is not mandated.

musescore.mechanism: Parts can receive independent styles and layout treatment within the project.

mei.mechanism: Part structures and linking can retain relationships; layout policy belongs to the rendering workflow.

features.question: A notation file and a measured performance transcript answer different questions.

krn.mechanism: Humdrum can carry performance events alongside **kern; note-on/off data is a separate representation.

musicxml.mechanism: attack, release and dynamics can qualify the performance of a notated note.
musicxml.caveat: Not every player consumes these fields.

musescore.mechanism: The project includes playback controls, but it is not a full performance-analysis interchange model.
musescore.caveat: Supported controls vary by sound engine.

mei.mechanism: MEI offers performed duration, real-time timestamps and velocity-related data alongside notation.

features.question: One trill sign can admit several historically plausible performances.

krn.mechanism: **kern encodes ornament signs; a realised performance needs extra events/data.

musicxml.mechanism: Sound-oriented information can accompany notation, but a symbol does not specify a unique realisation.

musescore.mechanism: Ornaments have application playback settings and behaviours.
musescore.caveat: Preserve an explicit realisation separately if exact notes are required.

mei.mechanism: Notated material and an expanded/gestural reading can be recorded separately.
mei.caveat: Consumer policy determines which representation is played.

features.feature: Dynamics affecting one voice on a shared stave
features.question: The position of a dynamic does not reliably identify its playback scope.

krn.mechanism: **dyn / **dynam distinguish notated and interpreted dynamics.
krn.caveat: Specify how the stream associates with musical voices.

musicxml.mechanism: direction can include voice; scope and actual playback should be checked in the recipient.
musicxml.caveat: A printed placement is not a voice selector.

musescore.mechanism: Dynamics can target a specific voice, all voices on a staff, or the instrument.
musescore.caveat: This capability belongs to later MuseScore 4 builds, not every 4.x release.

mei.mechanism: dynam carries layer, staff and event/timestamp references.
mei.caveat: Targeted encoding does not promise per-layer playback in every tool.

features.question: A Ped. line is not a sampled half-pedal trajectory.

krn.mechanism: Keep continuous/controller data in a suitable associated performance representation.
krn.caveat: Core **kern alone is not that controller stream.

musicxml.mechanism: Playback parameters are distinct from graphical directions.
musicxml.caveat: Do not assume the format substitutes for arbitrary DAW automation.

musescore.mechanism: Pedal lines/symbols have engraving controls; playback depends on the instrument and engine.
musescore.caveat: Continuous half-pedal fidelity was not tested.

mei.mechanism: MEI can supplement the score with performance information.
mei.caveat: Consumer support for continuous control must be established.

features.feature: Align the score with an audio/video recording
features.question: A recording link alone does not identify the moment corresponding to a note.

krn.mechanism: Humdrum’s sound-analysis workflow can coexist with custom alignment streams.
krn.caveat: Document the event-address and time-unit convention.

musicxml.mechanism: Use linked resources plus a separate mapping of score events to recording times.
musicxml.caveat: Generic links are not a rich recording-alignment model.

musescore.mechanism: Exported audio/video is a rendering, not a general alignment of an independently recorded performance.

mei.mechanism: Performance structures and temporal references support alignment with recordings.

features.feature: Virtual instruments, effects and mixer state
features.question: Preserve a production setup separately from portable score semantics.

krn.mechanism: Humdrum can generate synthesis/performance data; a plugin rack is outside core **kern.

musicxml.mechanism: sound/play carry instrument and technique information, not a universal plugin-host project.

musescore.mechanism: The mixer selects SoundFonts, VST instruments or MuseSounds and supports effects.
musescore.caveat: Required sounds/plugins must be available in the target environment.

mei.mechanism: MEI can describe performance data and recordings; it is not a standard VST host-session package.

features.question: A valid file can still encode the wrong music or lose the intended interpretation.

krn.mechanism: Use syntax/representation checks plus musical and source review.
krn.caveat: There is no single check that proves the transcription correct.

musicxml.mechanism: The published schema checks structure and types.
musicxml.caveat: It cannot prove voicing, rhythmic intention or successful interchange.

musescore.mechanism: Opening in the intended build is a practical compatibility check.
musescore.caveat: No independent comprehensive native-format validator was established here.

mei.mechanism: Validate against the declared MEI customization, then verify musical and editorial constraints.
mei.caveat: Schema validity is not renderer compatibility.

features.question: An importer may successfully open a file while discarding information it does not model.

krn.mechanism: Transformations may select or replace spines; retain custom-data definitions and original input.

musicxml.mechanism: other-notation explicitly permits non-interoperable extensions.
musicxml.caveat: A valid custom field is not a retention guarantee.

musescore.mechanism: The reviewed documentation does not establish preservation of unknown native elements or all imported editorial fields.

mei.mechanism: Software targeting a subset may ignore full-MEI information.
mei.caveat: Keep a master document and check exported content.

features.question: A→B→A should compare semantics, appearance and playback separately.

krn.mechanism: Pitch and structural conventions can change during conversion; written/sounding conversion is explicit in VHV.
krn.caveat: Check annotations and stream relationships as well as notes.

musicxml.mechanism: MuseScore’s handbook warns that layout cleanup is commonly required after MusicXML transfer.

musescore.mechanism: Use native projects for continuing application work and exports as derivatives.
musescore.caveat: MusicXML/MEI exports are not complete backups of the project.

mei.mechanism: Basic and repertoire customizations differ from full MEI.
mei.caveat: A successful score import need not preserve apparatus or facsimile relationships.

features.question: Automation availability is a tool ecosystem property, not an intrinsic file-format guarantee.

krn.mechanism: Humdrum tools support selection, transformation, analysis and conversions.

musicxml.mechanism: Standard XML tooling can transform/inspect MusicXML; musical conversion needs a music-aware library.

musescore.mechanism: MuseScore documents export and batch conversion options.
musescore.caveat: The page warns that some content was copied from the version 3 manual; test the exact build.

mei.mechanism: XML tooling supports queries and transformations; musical semantics require profile-aware processing.

features.feature: Corpus analysis and aligned derived features
features.question: The cost of extracting a usable event stream differs substantially.

krn.mechanism: Humdrum provides interval, rhythm, harmony and pattern-analysis workflows with aligned derived representations.

musicxml.mechanism: Reconstruct timing from the cursor, voice labels and durations before comparing events.
musicxml.caveat: File order is not simply onset order.

musescore.mechanism: A notation editor project is less direct as a portable analytical table.
musescore.workaround: Export a suitable symbolic representation, checking the required distinctions.

mei.mechanism: Analysis markup is available; choose apparatus branches and temporal interpretations before calculating statistics.

features.question: The preferred master depends on which losses would be unacceptable.

krn.mechanism: Useful for stream-based research when conventions and companion data are preserved.
krn.caveat: Retain sources and reference renderings.

musicxml.mechanism: Useful for broad notation interchange; test the features your project depends on.
musicxml.caveat: Keep native or scholarly masters where they contain additional information.

musescore.mechanism: Keep the native project for editing in MuseScore and archive a documented environment.
musescore.caveat: Also retain portable exports and approved output.

mei.mechanism: Useful when source relationships, variants and editorial acts are first-class requirements.
mei.caveat: Preserve schema customizations and linked assets.

features.question: Compression changes packaging, not the underlying musical expressivity.

krn.mechanism: Humdrum is line/field-oriented text with typed spines and record classes.

musicxml.mechanism: MXL uses a ZIP container and META-INF/container.xml to identify the score root and alternate renditions.

musescore.mechanism: MuseScore’s native project formats differ from MusicXML even though XML is involved.
musescore.caveat: Preserve the original package and associated resources.

mei.mechanism: MEI is XML; associated images and recordings may be separate resources.
mei.caveat: A .mei suffix alone does not specify the customization.

cases.title: An editorial sharp with a responsible editor
cases.subtitle: A displayed bracket is only the beginning.
cases.introduction: Suppose a manuscript has an F, and an editor proposes F-sharp for performance. Preserve the proposed pitch, the absence of the accidental in the source, who supplied it, and the reason. Do not confuse an editorial sharp with a courtesy sharp.
notes: KRN: in a VHV profile, declare an RDF editorial-accidental signifier. Add a separate responsibility/comment convention if that information must be queryable.
MusicXML: encode the altered pitch and an editorial accidental; level/footnote can explain the act. A witness-based apparatus requires additional conventions or external data.
MuseScore: create the intended notation and visible editorial treatment. Preserve responsibility and evidence in an apparatus instead of expecting the bracket to carry them.
MEI: retain the supplied accidental and attribution, and use choice or app when the original and alternative reading must both remain available.

snippets.note: Small original example. The declaration gives i its meaning; responsibility is still absent.
Fragment only: assumes divisions=1 and a surrounding part/measure. It encodes editorial appearance but not a full apparatus.

cases.title: Two rhythms on one stave
cases.subtitle: Voice identity is separate from chord membership and stem direction.
cases.introduction: Take one 4/4 bar with a whole-note bass and four quarter notes above it. The sustained bass and moving line must retain independent durations and voice identity.
notes: KRN: split one spine into subspines. A dot in the sustained branch is a null token, not a rest or a repeated attack.
MusicXML: encode one voice, move the cursor back four quarter-note units, then encode the other voice on the same staff.
MuseScore: use separate voice slots, usually 1 and 2. Flipping a stem is insufficient.
MEI: use two layers in a staff. Independent durations belong to those layers rather than one uniform-duration chord.

snippets.note: Original sketch using literal tabs. VHV staff/voice rendering is a consumer convention; this example was not run through a music renderer.

snippets.code:
<staff n="1">
  <layer n="1">
    <note pname="g" oct="4" dur="4"/>
    <note pname="a" oct="4" dur="4"/>
    <note pname="b" oct="4" dur="4"/>
    <note pname="c" oct="5" dur="4"/>
  </layer>
  <layer n="2">
    <note pname="c" oct="4" dur="1"/>
  </layer>
</staff>
snippets.note: Fragment only. Supply the MEI namespace, score definition and enclosing measure/document.

cases.title: 3/4 against 4/4, at the same pulse
cases.subtitle: Independent bar boundaries, not just different printed signatures.
cases.introduction: On a common quarter-note timeline, the 3/4 part has boundaries at 0, 3, 6, 9, 12; the 4/4 part at 0, 4, 8, 12. Their first common endpoint is 12. Contrast this with differently written metres whose entire bars are stretched to the same duration.
notes: KRN/VHV: use the union of boundary times, with invisible bar markers in the staff that does not actually start a new bar. Count local measures independently.
MusicXML: partwise non-controlling measures are designed for non-aligned left boundaries. Test whether the destination preserves them or forces a shared bar grid.
MuseScore: local signatures rescale to the global bar span. A common-grid workaround can produce the picture, but it changes structural measures and may affect numbering, rests, repeats and export.

MEI: preserve non-controlling barlines in a suitable part-oriented or unmeasured organisation. Do not assume that marking an ordinary shared measure as non-controlling automatically creates independent local bar containers. On a measure, MEI control describes the right boundary; MusicXML non-controlling describes the left.

test_plan.title: Editorial sharp with a responsible editor
test_plan.acceptance: Preserve pitch, editorial status, enclosure, attribution and source reading independently.

test_plan.title: Whole-note bass against four upper quarter notes
test_plan.acceptance: Preserve both onsets and durations, one staff and two independent voices.

test_plan.title: Five concurrent lines on one staff
test_plan.acceptance: Identify whether the target rejects, splits, merges or discards a voice.

test_plan.title: 3/4 against 4/4 for 12 quarter notes
test_plan.acceptance: Local boundaries remain 0/3/6/9/12 and 0/4/8/12 with the same quarter-note pulse.

test_plan.title: 18/16 against 3/4 with common bar span
test_plan.acceptance: Distinguish visual duration from performed ratio.

test_plan.title: Nested tuplet crossing a barline
test_plan.acceptance: Preserve durations, nesting and bracket endpoints separately.

test_plan.title: Transposing instrument with a courtesy microtonal accidental
test_plan.acceptance: Check written spelling, sounding pitch, glyph and courtesy status.

test_plan.title: Shared-stem chord split over two staves
test_plan.acceptance: Check note ownership, displayed staff, stems and beams.

test_plan.title: Two witness readings, one supplied note and one illegible note
test_plan.acceptance: Do not flatten alternatives into simultaneous events or turn a gap into a rest.

test_plan.title: A note linked to a manuscript image region
test_plan.acceptance: Preserve the image URI, region coordinates and durable note identity.

test_plan.title: Voice-specific dynamics with pedal and grace notes
test_plan.acceptance: Check target voice, controller behaviour and realised grace timing independently.

test_plan.title: Linked parts with individual layout changes
test_plan.acceptance: Compare native linkage, part inclusion, page breaks and full-score consistency.
